full_text_en:
Jilin Huiguan Investment Co., Ltd. and

Third Party Dongzheng Rongcheng Capital Management Co., Ltd. v.

Changchun Northeast Asia Logistics Co., Ltd. and Third Party Dong Zhanqin

Dispute over Company Dissolution

Ruling Summary

The purpose of company dissolution is to protect the legitimate rights and interests of minority shareholders, and its essence is that the continued existence of the company has lost its significance to minority shareholders, manifested as the inability of minority shareholders to participate in the company's decision-making, management, profit sharing, or even to freely transfer shares and withdraw from the company. When all other remedies are exhausted, dissolution of the company is the only option. A company should operate in a sound manner in accordance with the Company Law, and dissolution of the company is also a powerful measure to standardize the corporate governance structure.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2017) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 2148

Re-applicant (First Instance Third Party): Dong Zhanqin, female, born on February 5, 1957, Han ethnicity, residing at Room 503, Unit 4, Building 40, West Fourth Community, Nanguan District, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Agent ad litem: Yu Honghua, lawyer from Jilin Chuangyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Chunguang, lawyer from Beijing Weiheng (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Re-applicant (First Instance Defendant, Second Instance Appellant): Changchun Northeast Asia Logistics Co., Ltd. Domicile: Lot 118, 5th Floor, No. 57 Changjiang Road, Economic and Technological Development Zone, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Dong Zhanqin, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Manli, lawyer from Beijing Weiheng (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhu Chunguang, lawyer from Beijing Weiheng (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Respondent (First Instance Plaintiff, Second Instance Appellee): Jilin Huiguan Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 621 Changchun Street, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Yue Yingmao, Chairperson of the Company.

First Instance Third Party: Dongzheng Rongcheng Capital Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 601, 6th Floor, No. 28 Jinshifang Street, Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Song Dalong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Jin Tian, employee of the Company.

Re-applicants Dong Zhanqin and Changchun Northeast Asia Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Northeast Asia Company"), in connection with the case of dispute over company dissolution with Respondent Jilin Huiguan Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Huiguan Company") and First Instance Third Party Dongzheng Rongcheng Capital Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Dongzheng Company"), disagreeing with the civil judgment (2016) Ji Min Zhong No. 569 of the Jilin High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, which has now concluded.

Dong Zhanqin applied for retrial on the grounds that: 1. Northeast Asia Company has been continuously profitable, and the first and second instance courts erred in finding that the company's operation and management had experienced serious difficulties, that the corporate organs such as the shareholders' meeting, board of directors, and board of supervisors could not function normally, that the decision-making mechanism had failed, and that conflicts among shareholders had become irreconcilable, for lack of sufficient evidence. 2. The second instance court erred in finding that the continued existence of the company would cause material losses to Huiguan Company's shareholder rights and interests, for lack of basis. 3. The second instance court erred in finding that the major difficulties in the company's operation and management could not be resolved through other means, which was a misapprehension of facts. 4. The first and second instance courts erred in applying the law when ruling to dissolve Northeast Asia Company. Dong Zhanqin applied for retrial pursuant to Article 200, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Northeast Asia Company applied for retrial on the grounds that: 1. Northeast Asia Company's operations were not deadlocked, and no serious difficulties in operation and management had occurred. 2. There was no evidence showing that the continued existence of Northeast Asia Company would cause material losses to the shareholders' interests; Northeast Asia Company had been profitable for consecutive years. 3. Huiguan Company sought to dissolve the company to obtain high returns, and had not exhausted all judicial remedies to resolve the existing disputes; thus, the statutory condition that the dispute cannot be resolved through other means was not met. Northeast Asia Company applied for retrial pursuant to Article 200, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Huiguan Company submitted its opinions stating that the first and second instance courts correctly found the facts, with sufficient evidence, and correctly applied the law. The retrial applications of Dong Zhanqin and Northeast Asia Company lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

This Court holds that the focus of this case is whether Northeast Asia Company meets the statutory conditions for company dissolution.

First, regarding the application of law. Northeast Asia Company was incorporated on September 20, 2004. As of December 2015, the business registration of Northeast Asia Company showed that Huiguan Company held 44% of the shares, Dong Zhanqin held 51%, and Dongzheng Company held 5%. Huiguan Company petitioned for the dissolution of Northeast Asia Company on the grounds that the company's operation and management had experienced serious difficulties, its shareholder interests had suffered material damage, and the deadlock could not be resolved through other means. It should be noted that a limited liability company is an organization with autonomous decision-making and behavioral capacity. Although internal confrontation among members may cause mechanism failure and inability to operate, making it impossible for the company to form effective resolutions in decision-making and management and thus falling into deadlock, given the characteristic of perpetual existence, the state's public power must exercise caution when shareholders petition for the dissolution of a company. When conflicts between shareholders cannot be resolved through negotiation and neither party is willing or able to exit the company, forced dissolution becomes the only measure to protect shareholders' legitimate rights and interests. Therefore, Article 182 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a company experiences serious difficulties in its operation and management, and the continued existence thereof will cause material losses to the interests of the shareholders, and such difficulties cannot be resolved through other means, a shareholder holding 10% or more of the voting rights of all shareholders of the company may petition the People's Court to dissolve the company." Furthermore, Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II) specifies four situations that constitute the formal requirements for accepting a company dissolution lawsuit and the substantive standards for determining whether to dissolve the company: 1. The company has been unable to convene a shareholders' meeting or general meeting for two consecutive years or more, and the company's operation and management have experienced serious difficulties; 2. The shareholders cannot reach the statutory or quorum required by the articles of association when voting, and have been unable to make effective shareholders' meeting or general meeting resolutions for two consecutive years or more, and the company's operation and management have experienced serious difficulties; 3. There has been long-term conflict among the company's directors, which cannot be resolved through the shareholders' meeting or general meeting, and the company's operation and management have experienced serious difficulties; 4. Other serious difficulties in operation and management have occurred, and the continued existence of the company will cause material losses to the interests of the shareholders. In company dissolution cases, the law does not require the shareholder seeking dissolution to exercise any specific right as a precondition for petitioning the People's Court to dissolve the company. The first and second instance courts, in accordance with Article 182 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 1, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II), based on the facts found, and after multiple unsuccessful mediations, made a judgment to dissolve Northeast Asia Company in order to fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of the company's shareholders, standardize the corporate governance structure, and promote the healthy development of the market economy. The application of law was not improper.

Second, regarding whether Northeast Asia Company meets the statutory conditions for company dissolution. (A) The operation and management of Northeast Asia Company have experienced serious difficulties. Whether a company's operation and management have experienced serious difficulties should be comprehensively analyzed from the operational status of the company's organizational structure. Whether the company is profitable is not a necessary condition for determining that its operation and management have experienced serious difficulties. The focus is on whether there are serious internal obstacles in the company's operation and management, whether the shareholders' meeting or board of directors is deadlocked due to intensifying conflicts, and whether one party's shareholders are unable to effectively participate in the company's operation and management. In this case, a comprehensive analysis can be made from three aspects: the board of directors, the shareholders' meeting, and the board of supervisors. According to the facts found by the first and second instance courts: Regarding the board of directors, the board of Northeast Asia Company had five members, with three from Dong Zhanqin's side and two from Huiguan Company's side. Article 53 of the company's articles of association provides: "The board of directors shall exercise voting rights on behalf of the shareholders when making decisions. Resolutions on matters discussed at board meetings shall be adopted by directors representing three-fifths or more (including the number) of the voting rights." According to this provision, proposals from Dong Zhanqin's side could be passed without the consent of Huiguan Company's side. Huiguan Company had proposed amending the articles of association three times, each time rejected by Dong Zhanqin. Additionally, when Huiguan Company sought to transfer part of its shares to Dongzheng Company, Northeast Asia Company refused to cooperate, and the transfer was only realized through litigation. Since August 6, 2013, Northeast Asia Company had not convened a board meeting for two years, and the board had long ceased to function properly. Regarding the shareholders' meeting, since February 3, 2015, Northeast Asia Company had not convened a shareholders' meeting for two years, could not form effective resolutions, and was unable to resolve the intense conflicts among directors through the shareholders' meeting. The shareholders' meeting mechanism had failed. Regarding the board of supervisors, since its establishment, Northeast Asia Company had never convened a meeting of the board of supervisors, and the supervisors had not exercised their supervisory powers in accordance with the Company Law or the articles of association. In summary, objectively, the board of directors of Northeast Asia Company was controlled by Dong Zhanqin's side, and Huiguan Company could not normally exercise its shareholder rights or participate in operation and management by appointing directors to the board. The internal organs of Northeast Asia Company could not function normally, and the company's operation and management were deadlocked. (B) The continued existence of Northeast Asia Company will cause material losses to the shareholder rights and interests of Huiguan Company. Shareholders of a company are entitled by law to select managers, participate in major decisions, and receive dividends. In this case, Huiguan Company could not normally appoint managers. On August 29, 2007, Huiguan Company recommended Chang Liguo as General Manager; on March 11, 2015, Huiguan Company appointed Song Dalong and Xu Fengjiu as directors and as Vice Chairperson and Deputy General Manager, respectively. Northeast Asia Company refused both appointments on the grounds that they did not meet the three-fifths decision-making ratio required by the articles of association. The power of personnel appointment and removal in Northeast Asia Company was entirely in the hands of Dong Zhanqin. Huiguan Company could not normally participate in major corporate decisions. Northeast Asia Company borrowed RMB 72.22 million from Dong Zhanqin personally, without any corresponding shareholders' meeting or board resolution. Additionally, an audit report showed that Dong Zhanqin's related parties had borrowed nearly RMB 100 million from Northeast Asia Company. In October 2014, Northeast Asia Company applied for a RMB 50 million loan from Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, but Huiguan Company was unaware of the purpose of the loan. In 2015, when Northeast Asia Company carried out renovation and expansion of its grain and oil market, Huiguan Company and its appointed directors did not participate. Huiguan Company did not receive profits from Northeast Asia Company. Although Northeast Asia Company claimed to be continuously profitable, it had not distributed dividends for many years. As the second largest shareholder of Northeast Asia Company, Huiguan Company had long been unable to normally exercise its shareholder rights to participate in the company's operation decisions, management, supervision, and selection of managers. The contractual purpose of Huiguan Company's investment in Northeast Asia Company could not be achieved, and its shareholder rights and interests suffered material losses. (C) The conflicts among the shareholders of Northeast Asia Company cannot be resolved through other means. Based on the personal nature of a limited liability company, shareholders should be mutually accommodating and actively and rationally resolve conflicts. After conflicts arose between the shareholders of Northeast Asia Company, Huiguan Company attempted to change the company's decision-making mechanism by amending the articles of association to resolve the disputes, or to exit the company by transferring its shares to Dong Zhanqin to end the deadlock, but all efforts failed. Even the partial transfer of shares to Dongzheng Company could only be realized through litigation due to the conflicts between Huiguan Company and Dong Zhanqin. Moreover, the first instance court, cautious about using judicial means to force dissolution, organized multiple mediations among the parties. During the mediation at the second instance, Huiguan Company and Dongzheng Company proposed to assess the asset value of Northeast Asia Company, determine the share price, and have Dong Zhanqin acquire the shares of Huiguan Company and Dongzheng Company in Northeast Asia Company, with Huiguan Company and Dongzheng Company exiting the company. Ultimately, the parties failed to reach an agreement, and mediation was unsuccessful. The deadlock in Northeast Asia Company could not be resolved through other means. In summary, the long-standing conflicts among the shareholders and directors of Northeast Asia Company have destroyed the trust basis for continued cooperation. The decision-making and management mechanisms of the company have failed. The continued existence of the company will inevitably harm the major interests of Huiguan Company, and the deadlock cannot be resolved through other means. The conditions for Huiguan Company to insist on dissolution of Northeast Asia Company have been met.

In conclusion, the retrial applications of Dong Zhanqin and Northeast Asia Company do not meet the circumstances provided in Article 200, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 395, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The retrial applications of Dong Zhanqin and Changchun Northeast Asia Logistics Co., Ltd. are dismissed.
